items.articleText: New Project Lead for ROS PMC! - Projects - Open Robotics Discourse New Project Lead for ROS PMC! Projects ros2 , pmc ahcorde October 26, 2026, 9:00am 1 Hello ROS Community! I’m Alejandro Hernández Cordero (@ahcorde ), and I’m happy to share that the ROS PMC has selected me as the new ROS project lead. It’s an honor to take on this role for a project that has shaped so much of my career. First, a big thank you to Michael Carroll (@mjcarroll ). He took on the interim role at a moment of change, shipped Kilted and Lyrical, and worked with the TGC to define what the project lead role should look like. That work made this transition possible, and I’m grateful to be building on the foundation he left. A bit about me: I wrote my first ROS node in 2012 for my master’s final project, and I never really left. I spent several years at Open Robotics maintaining ROS 2 core packages and the ROS 2 and Gazebo integration, and today I’m at Honu Robotics , where I see every day what it takes to bring ROS from a prototype to a real product. A lot of what I know about ROS I learned in review threads, from people all over the world, and that collaborative spirit is something I want to protect and grow. What I’ll be working on: Shipping ROS 2 Makoa Mata-mata on World Turtle Day, May 23, 2027, with a release process that is predictable and easy to follow. Growing the maintainer base, so ROS doesn’t depend on a handful of people, and making the path from first contribution to maintainer clearer. Keeping ROS and Gazebo working smoothly together, from simulation to real robots. Working with OSRA members, the TGC and the PMC on the project’s priorities, and making sure the community’s voice is part of those decisions. How you can help: join a PMC meeting (observers are welcome, and the minutes are public), get involved with a working group, or pick up an issue on GitHub. Reviewing pull requests, improving documentation and answering questions are just as valuable as writing code. Discourse and Discord are great places to start a conversation, and if you’re not sure where to begin, ask, and we’ll help you find a good fit. My door is open. Reach out on Discourse, GitHub (ahcorde (Alejandro Hernández Cordero) · GitHub ) or LinkedIn (Alejandro Hernández Cordero - Intrinsic | LinkedIn ) with ideas, questions or concerns. I’d especially like to hear from people using ROS in production, in research and in the classroom about what’s working and what isn’t. Let’s keep building! items.title: RoboStack moved to a Monorepo
items.summary: Hi everyone, RoboStack has moved to a monorepo approach! You can read all about it in this document . Why? All the major distros are now managed from one repo. This removes a lot of duplication and makes maintaining the distro channels much easier. Patches, new packages, testing and rebuilds can now be done for all distros at once, in a single PR. Easier to contribute We added several features to help new maintainers get started. The biggest one is the new robostack-bot . It takes care of some of the regular maintenance work and can generate PR’s for standardized functions like adding a new package. You can ask it for help by commenting @robostack-bot add-package <pkg>... [<distro>...] on GitHub. Is your package already there? Check the package lists, for example for Lyrical: ROS 2 Lyrical | RoboStack If something is missing, open an issue and the bot can help get it added. Feedback and new contributors are very welcome! 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic

items.title: Bedrock Robotics nears $1B in total funding as demand for autonomous heavy equipment surges
items.summary: Bedrock Robotics has secured $600 million to scale autonomous heavy equipment and combat construction labor shortages. The post Bedrock Robotics nears $1B in total funding as demand for autonomous heavy equipment surges appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: Bedrock Robotics automates large excavators to improve construction site economics. | Credit: Bedrock Robotics San Francisco-based Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in Series C funding, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, at a $4.1 billion valuation. The round brings its total funding to nearly $1 billion as it scales fully autonomous heavy equipment to address nationwide construction labor shortages. The round included new investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Bessemer Venture Partners, and Temasek, alongside existing investors 8VC, Georgian, Valor Equity Partners, Xora, Eclipse, Perry Creek Capital, NVIDIA, and others. Bedrock said this will accelerate the deployment of Bedrock-equipped machines across commercial construction sites across the U.S., helping contractors use existing heavy equipment more safely, predictably, and at greater capacity. The new capital follows a rapid commercial expansion beyond the company ’s initial footprint in the West and Central South into the Midwest and South Atlantic. Anchored by a major partnership with Southwest contractor Haydon to automate earthwork in Texas, Bedrock has added regional partners across Minnesota, Florida, Georgia, Missouri, and Virginia—pushing its autonomous retrofits onto live job sites spanning data centers, healthcare facilities, and heavy civil infrastructure. “We have proven that fully autonomous excavators can perform real work of value alongside the crews and workflows already in place on job sites,” said Boris Sofman, co-founder and CEO of Bedrock Robotics. “The next challenge is delivering that capability to more contractors as a dependable part of how projects get built.” “This funding allows us to expand deployments, strengthen the field operations behind every machine, and work with more partners as they integrate intelligent systems into everyday work,” he added. “The opportunity is to help the industry’s experienced crews safely take on more projects, deliver with greater consistency, and quickly deliver more of the infrastructure this country needs.” Sofman told The Robot Report , “New customer demand is very high. We’re responsibly growing into the demand, bringing on new customers we can serve alongside our longtime design partners. We’re scaling across the board, from operations to hardware to supply chain operations, to keep pace with the needs of our customers.” Bedrock Robotics adds leadership In the midst of securing new funding, the company also added two new individuals to the management team. Amy Jones Satrom joins the leadership team as vice president of operations. She brings operations experience from Amazon, Nuro, and Uber to lead the company in the next phase of scaling to meet demand. “Amy is instrumental in strengthening our operations and building the systems and support that make successful deployments repeatable,” according to Sofman. “She’s still early in her tenure, but her leadership will be central to growing our deployment and production teams and preparing them to support customers across the country. “Ajay Gummalla, a co-founder and VP of engineering, is also intimately involved on the hardware side of things, adding resilience to our supply chain so we’re ready to build the hardware we need to meet customer demand,” he explained. Lando Juarez has joined Bedrock Robotics in the role of general counsel. He was formerly head of legal for Uber’s Autonomous Mobility & Delivery business, overseeing commercial partnerships and regulatory pathways. Submit your innovation now! Looking to the future of construction When asked bout how the company is planning to grow, Sofman responded, “Short term, our growth market remains construction. It is a massive market — 4% to 5% of U.S. GDP — so we’re thinking about expanding use cases. Haydon will test our excavators for autonomous trench work.” “We’re also thinking about automating larger machine models — Haydon and others will explore bulldozers, ADTs, and wheel loaders as possible heavy machines to automate next,” he said. “Long term: We’re looking at the other industries, like mining and agriculture, that are 1) also dealing with labor constraints and 2) use the same kinds of heavy machines GCs do.” “For 2027, we are relentlessly focused on getting more Bedrock-equipped machines on more job sites around the country,” Sofman continued. “It was just a few months ago that we first launched fully autonomous excavators on live, commercial job sites, just two years after Bedrock came out of stealth. 2027 is about doubling down on that progress, getting to triple-digit machines working autonomously across the country.” When asked about the installed base and economic opportunity for Bedrock Robotics’ systems, Sofman was more reserved. “It’s a bit early to give concrete numbers,” said Sofman, “However, given the labor constraints on general contractors, the math pencils out: Imagine a job that can be completed two months faster because autonomous machines are running around the clock, seven days a week.” “The developer paying 9% interest on a $400 million loan would save $6 million on that project they can invest into future projects,” he observed. “In turn, construction crews and all the downstream trades, like plumbing and electrical, would see an increasing volume of steady work because there are more projects that can be funded.” Some data on labor constraints that have opened the market for Bedrock: Twenty percent of construction workers are over the age of 55, and estimates suggest that more than 40% of the construction workers will retire in the next five years. Large projects already run an average of 20% over schedule and 80% over budget. In construction specifically, 87% of firms report openings for hourly craft positions, and 88% say the roles are as hard or harder to fill than a year ago. With 25+ years of experience, including leadership roles at Adept Technology, Mike founded the Mobile Robot Guide (acquired by WTWH). items.title: OMRON to acquire OnLogic to address edge AI applications
items.summary: OMRON will add industrial computing from OnLogic to its industrial automation expertise to serve data- and AI-intensive applications. The post OMRON to acquire OnLogic to address edge AI applications appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: OnLogic will keep its Vermont headquarters, as well as its global offices, as part of OMRON. Source: OnLogic As manufacturers increasingly use data and AI at the edge, they need reliable computing that works alongside real-time automation and control. OMRON Corp. this month said it has agreed to acquire 100% of OnLogic this week, worth $675 million, to combine its proven automation with OnLogic’s industrial computing expertise. “This acquisition is an important step in advancing our SF2030 vision and our evolution toward GEMBA DX,” stated Junta Tsujinaga, president and CEO of OMRON. “North America is a key growth market for OMRON, and this investment strengthens our foundation there while building the capabilities our customers will increasingly need.” “OnLogic’s industrial computing expertise, flexibility and strong customer relationships complement our strengths in automation and control,” he added. “Together, we see an opportunity to create new value for customers as manufacturing becomes more connected, data-driven and intelligent.” Founded in 1933, OMRON Automation creates, sells, and services fully integrated automation solutions that include sensing , control , safety , vision , and motion . The Kyoto, Japan-based company said its 30,000 employees creatively help businesses solve problems in more than 110 countries. Its Americas office is in Hoffman Estates, Ill. Submit your innovation now! OnLogic to continue computing brand Founded in 2003, OnLogic designs and makes configurable, solution-focused, AI -capable computers engineered for reliability at the Internet of Things (IoT ) edge. The South Burlington, Vt.-based company said it has helped more than 70,000 customers worldwide with their complex computing challenges with systems that are built to order, delivered in days, and designed to last. OnLogic noted that its systems operate in the world’s harshest environments across industries. It said joining OMRON will provide industrial automation expertise and access to new markets. “We built OnLogic to help engineers and innovators solve tough technology challenges by making custom, rugged hardware easy to configure, build, and deploy,” said Sean Larkin, CEO of OnLogic. “Joining OMRON provides the global scale, supply chain depth, and capital resources to accelerate our product roadmaps while preserving our culture, direct sales approach, and operations around the world. Together, we are giving our customers the tools they need to deploy physical AI with confidence.” Following the acquisition, OnLogic will continue to operate as an independent business within the OMRON Group. It will keep its offices in the U.S., the Netherlands, Germany, Taiwan, and Malaysia, as well as its brand identity and direct sales model. OnLogic’s management team, led by Larkin, will remain in place to drive day-to-day operations and strategic growth. OMRON sees opportunities for manufacturers The companies said they will help customers address increasingly complex applications that require greater processing power, connectivity, and intelligence at the edge. OMRON has experience in control, robotics, and safety. OnLogic brings configurable computing platforms designed for demanding applications and environments, as well as its flexible build-to-order model and customer reach across manufacturing and other markets. The companies said they expect to more closely connect machine data, edge computing, and AI with real-time automation and control. Over time, the combination is expected to create systems that help turn data, insights, and AI into faster, more informed actions to optimize manufacturing. OMRON added that the acquisition is an investment in its Industrial Automation Business and strengthens the company’s position in the Americas and Europe . OnLogic has relationships with customers across both traditional automation markets and industries where OMRON sees additional opportunities for growth. In addition, OMRON said it remains committed to its established channel strategy and to continuing to invest in and support the partners that help it serve customers and grow in the market. items.title: Agility and GXO Logistics plan expanded deployment of Digit humanoid
items.summary: GXO Logistics, which has tested humanoid robots from multiple companies, will deploy Agility's Digit at two more sites. The post Agility and GXO Logistics plan expanded deployment of Digit humanoid appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: Agility and GXO have been collaborating since 2023. Source: Agility Robotics Agility Robotics and GXO Logistics today said they are expanding their partnership to deploy Agility’s Digit humanoid robot in GXO sites in North Carolina and Tennessee. “GXO was the first customer to put Digit to work in live operations under a commercial agreement, and expanding to additional sites is the clearest signal that the value is real,” stated Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility. “Customers are moving beyond asking whether humanoid robots can work to deciding where they can scale them. Years of experience performing real work in GXO’s operations have shaped how we build, deploy and support Digit, and we’re focused on disciplined execution as we grow this partnership.” Founded in 2015, Agility Robotics said it has more than 65,000 hours of real-world operation working with industry safety standards. The Salem, Ore.-based company recently got U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approval for its planned merger with special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC ) Churchill Capital Corp. XI as it prepares to go public. In 2024, Digit earned Agility the inaugural RBR50 Robot of the Year award for being one of the first humanoids to enter commercial trials. It received 2026 honors for moving more than 100,000 totes for GXO last year. This month, the company chose Nyobolt for fast charging , expanded its partnership with NVIDIA, and said it plans to deploy Digit at an AGCO factory for agricultural equipment in 2027. Submit your innovation now! GXO and Agility continue collaboration Spun out of XPO Inc. in 2021, GXO Logistics claimed that it is “the world’s largest pure-play contract logistics provider.” The third-party logistics provider (3PL ) has more than 150,000 employees across over 1,000 facilities, totaling more than 200 million sq. ft. (18.5 million sq. m). The Greenwich, Conn.-based company last month partnered with Exotec to automate fulfillment for Guess in the Netherlands, and like Agility , its executives participated in keynote panels last week’s RoboBusiness event. GXO and Agility first deployed Digit in late 2023 in at a facility in Flowery Branch, Ga. The companies asserted that it was the industry’s first commercial deployment of humanoid robots in live operations and the first robotics-as-a-service (RaaS ) agreement for humanoid robots. Since then, Digit has moved more than 100,000 totes at the Flowery Branch facility, demonstrating its ability to perform repetitive material handling tasks reliably in an active logistics environment. The robot uses the Agility Arc cloud-based fleet management and integration platform. It has worked alongside existing automation to move totes and place them onto conveyors. “Innovation is most powerful when it delivers practical solutions that create value for our customers and our people,” said GXO CEO Patrick Kelleher. “Our partnership with Agility Robotics has been defined by a shared commitment to turning emerging technologies into real-world operational advantage. Together, we’ve helped pioneer the use of humanoid robotics in the warehouse and this expansion reflects our confidence in the technology’s ability to create measurable value for our customers and a better working environment for our teams.” Digit will move from handling bins to more applications. Source: Agility GXO Logistics has tested other humanoids GXO has also tested humanoid robots including Apollo from Apptronik and Reflex from Reflex Robotics . In the company’s second-quarter earnings call in August, Kelleher acknowledged that it had not yet deployed humanoids in production, nor had they produced a return on investment (ROI). “We’ve done 45 pilots on humanoids so far. We have an additional pilot launching in Europe very shortly,” he said at the time. “We have not achieved ROI on humanoids yet. I think we are a couple of years away from that, but we’re seeing such great progress with our partners around the efficacy of that technology and the application opportunities that it has in the warehouse environment.” GXO did not say how much it is investing in the Digit expansion or when and if it expects ROI. The Robot Report has reached out and will share any additional comment or clarification. Partners plan to deploy Digit to more U.S. sites Under the expanded agreement, Digit will support e-commerce fulfillment at GXO sites in Statesville, Tenn., and Lebanon, Ind. The companies said they expect to begin deployments of Digit 4 in in early 2027. Digit 5, which Agility unveiled last month, is designed with new legs, to operate safely near people, and to address a wider range of industrial workflows. GXO said it will migrate to Digit 5 when it becomes commercially available. “The expansion reflects GXO’s long-standing approach to advancing warehouse automation through practical implementation at scale,” said GXO. “As an industry leader in advanced automation and physical AI, GXO partners with leading technology developers to test, refine and deploy emerging solutions in live operating environments. The expanded partnership underscores GXO’s and Agility’s shared commitment to accelerating innovation through real-world application and continuous learning.” Agility also noted that it has invested in infrastructure to manufacture, deploy, and support humanoid robots at scale, including its 70,000 sq. ft. (6,503.2 sq. m) RoboFab facility to manufacture up to 10,000 robots per year. The company has also expanded software and service capabilities, as well as announced plans for a new 50,000 sq. ft. (4,645 sq. m) facility in Pittsburgh to support commercial deployments. A spokesperson told The Robot Report that Agility has paid programs with a global automaker, a major automotive component supplier, and a global consumer products maker. The company said it has more than 30 prospective customers in its pipeline across manufacturing, logistics, aerospace, defense, and consumer products. He was senior editor of The Robot Report from 2019 to 2020 and editorial director of Robotics 24/7 from 2020 to 2023. Prior to working at Arrowfly, Demaitre was an editor at BNA (now part of Bloomberg), Computerworld, TechTarget, and Robotics Business Review. report.one_sentence_summary: RoboStack의 모노레포 전환 및 BTick 디버깅 도구 공개와 함께 Greptile·CodeRabbit의 최신 AI 모델 기반 코드 분석 적용, Bedrock Robotics 투자 및 OMRON 인수가 진행되었습니다.
report.cross_insight: - 해석: AI 기반 소프트웨어 개발 도구들이 단순 코드 완성을 넘어 GPT-6 계열 모델을 활용한 런타임 워크플로 결함 탐지 및 복잡한 코드베이스의 보안 위험 분석으로 자동화 범위를 확장하고 있습니다 [6, 8].
report.section_robotics:
- **RoboStack**: 주요 배포판 관리를 단일 리포지토리에서 수행하는 모노레포 구조로 전환하고 단일 PR 일괄 빌드 및 패키지 추가를 지원하는 robostack-bot을 도입했습니다 [2].
- **BTick**: BehaviorTree.CPP 애플리케이션의 실시간 모니터링, 중단점 설정 기반 대화형 디버깅, 런타임 제어 및 Nav2 로깅 토픽 연동을 지원하는 시각화 도구가 공개되었습니다 [4].
report.section_devtools:
- **Greptile**: 코드 리뷰 단계를 넘어 사용자 워크플로를 테스트하고 버그 탐지 범위를 확장하기 위해 GPT-6 Astra를 도입했습니다 [6].
- **OpenAI**: 카케야 추측, 지수 시간 가설, 양자색역학 연구에서 도출된 모델 결과와 연구자 검증 방안을 과학 커뮤니티와 공유했습니다 [7].
- **CodeRabbit**: 복잡한 코드베이스 전반의 보안 위험을 조사하고 취약점 검토 및 수정을 지원하기 위해 GPT-6.1 Sol 기반 보안 에이전트를 적용했습니다 [8].
- **Hob**: Mac, Windows, Linux 환경에서 외부 API 의존 없이 Gemma 및 gpt-oss 등 오픈 가중치 모델을 오프라인 로컬로 구동하는 무료 오픈소스 데스크톱 애플리케이션이 공개되었습니다 [11].
report.section_industry:
- **Bedrock Robotics**: 건설 현장 인력난에 대응한 자율 중장비 개조 및 상용 배치를 위해 41억 달러 기업가치로 6억 달러 규모의 시리즈 C 투자를 유치했습니다 [13].
- **OMRON**: 산업 현장의 엣지 AI 역량 강화를 목적으로 산업용 컴퓨팅 제조 기업 OnLogic의 지분 100%를 6억 7,500만 달러에 인수하기로 합의했습니다 [14].
- **Agility Robotics**: GXO Logistics와의 파트너십을 확장하여 물류 물품 이송 현장인 노스캐롤라이나와 테네시 거점에 Digit 휴머노이드 로봇 추가 배치를 추진합니다 [15].

selectedItems.title: RoboStack moved to a Monorepo
selectedItems.summary: Hi everyone, RoboStack has moved to a monorepo approach! You can read all about it in this document . Why? All the major distros are now managed from one repo. This removes a lot of duplication and makes maintaining the distro channels much easier. Patches, new packages, testing and rebuilds can now be done for all distros at once, in a single PR. Easier to contribute We added several features to help new maintainers get started. The biggest one is the new robostack-bot . It takes care of some of the regular maintenance work and can generate PR’s for standardized functions like adding a new package. You can ask it for help by commenting @robostack-bot add-package <pkg>... [<distro>...] on GitHub. Is your package already there? Check the package lists, for example for Lyrical: ROS 2 Lyrical | RoboStack If something is missing, open an issue and the bot can help get it added. Feedback and new contributors are very welcome! 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic

Integrated XML Editor — Create and edit BehaviorTree.CPP v4 XML files with interactive visualization and navigation. Three Protocols & Integrations BTick Protocol — Native monitoring and interactive debugging. Groot2 Protocol — Groot2-compatible communication and supported Pro features. selectedItems.title: Bedrock Robotics nears $1B in total funding as demand for autonomous heavy equipment surges
selectedItems.summary: Bedrock Robotics has secured $600 million to scale autonomous heavy equipment and combat construction labor shortages. The post Bedrock Robotics nears $1B in total funding as demand for autonomous heavy equipment surges appeared first on The Robot Report .
selectedItems.articleText: Bedrock Robotics automates large excavators to improve construction site economics. | Credit: Bedrock Robotics San Francisco-based Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in Series C funding, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, at a $4.1 billion valuation. The round brings its total funding to nearly $1 billion as it scales fully autonomous heavy equipment to address nationwide construction labor shortages. The round included new investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Bessemer Venture Partners, and Temasek, alongside existing investors 8VC, Georgian, Valor Equity Partners, Xora, Eclipse, Perry Creek Capital, NVIDIA, and others. Bedrock said this will accelerate the deployment of Bedrock-equipped machines across commercial construction sites across the U.S., helping contractors use existing heavy equipment more safely, predictably, and at greater capacity. The new capital follows a rapid commercial expansion beyond the company ’s initial footprint in the West and Central South into the Midwest and South Atlantic. Anchored by a major partnership with Southwest contractor Haydon to automate earthwork in Texas, Bedrock has added regional partners across Minnesota, Florida, Georgia, Missouri, and Virginia—pushing its autonomous retrofits onto live job sites spanning data centers, healthcare facilities, and heavy civil infrastructure. “We have proven that fully autonomous excavators can perform real work of value alongside the crews and workflows already in place on job sites,” said Boris Sofman, co-founder and CEO of Bedrock Robotics. “The next challenge is delivering that capability to more contractors as a dependable part of how projects get built.” “This funding allows us to expand deployments, strengthen the field operations behind every machine, and work with more partners as they integrate intelligent systems into everyday work,” he added. “The opportunity is to help the industry’s experienced crews safely take on more projects, deliver with greater consistency, and quickly deliver more of the infrastructure this country needs.” Sofman told The Robot Report , “New customer demand is very high. We’re responsibly growing into the demand, bringing on new customers we can serve alongside our longtime design partners. We’re scaling across the board, from operations to hardware to supply chain operations, to keep pace with the needs of our customers.” Bedrock Robotics adds leadership In the midst of securing new funding, the company also added two new individuals to the management team. Amy Jones Satrom joins the leadership team as vice president of operations. She brings operations experience from Amazon, Nuro, and Uber to lead the company in the next phase of scaling to meet demand. “Amy is instrumental in strengthening our operations and building the systems and support that make successful deployments repeatable,” according to Sofman. “She’s still early in her tenure, but her leadership will be central to growing our deployment and production teams and preparing them to support customers across the country. “Ajay Gummalla, a co-founder and VP of engineering, is also intimately involved on the hardware side of things, adding resilience to our supply chain so we’re ready to build the hardware we need to meet customer demand,” he explained. Lando Juarez has joined Bedrock Robotics in the role of general counsel. He was formerly head of legal for Uber’s Autonomous Mobility & Delivery business, overseeing commercial partnerships and regulatory pathways. Submit your innovation now! Looking to the future of construction When asked bout how the company is planning to grow, Sofman responded, “Short term, our growth market remains construction. It is a massive market — 4% to 5% of U.S. GDP — so we’re thinking about expanding use cases. Haydon will test our excavators for autonomous trench work.” “We’re also thinking about automating larger machine models — Haydon and others will explore bulldozers, ADTs, and wheel loaders as possible heavy machines to automate next,” he said. “Long term: We’re looking at the other industries, like mining and agriculture, that are 1) also dealing with labor constraints and 2) use the same kinds of heavy machines GCs do.” “For 2027, we are relentlessly focused on getting more Bedrock-equipped machines on more job sites around the country,” Sofman continued. “It was just a few months ago that we first launched fully autonomous excavators on live, commercial job sites, just two years after Bedrock came out of stealth. 2027 is about doubling down on that progress, getting to triple-digit machines working autonomously across the country.” When asked about the installed base and economic opportunity for Bedrock Robotics’ systems, Sofman was more reserved. “It’s a bit early to give concrete numbers,” said Sofman, “However, given the labor constraints on general contractors, the math pencils out: Imagine a job that can be completed two months faster because autonomous machines are running around the clock, seven days a week.” “The developer paying 9% interest on a $400 million loan would save $6 million on that project they can invest into future projects,” he observed. “In turn, construction crews and all the downstream trades, like plumbing and electrical, would see an increasing volume of steady work because there are more projects that can be funded.” Some data on labor constraints that have opened the market for Bedrock: Twenty percent of construction workers are over the age of 55, and estimates suggest that more than 40% of the construction workers will retire in the next five years. Large projects already run an average of 20% over schedule and 80% over budget. In construction specifically, 87% of firms report openings for hourly craft positions, and 88% say the roles are as hard or harder to fill than a year ago. selectedItems.title: OMRON to acquire OnLogic to address edge AI applications
selectedItems.summary: OMRON will add industrial computing from OnLogic to its industrial automation expertise to serve data- and AI-intensive applications. The post OMRON to acquire OnLogic to address edge AI applications appeared first on The Robot Report .
selectedItems.articleText: OnLogic will keep its Vermont headquarters, as well as its global offices, as part of OMRON. Source: OnLogic As manufacturers increasingly use data and AI at the edge, they need reliable computing that works alongside real-time automation and control. OMRON Corp. this month said it has agreed to acquire 100% of OnLogic this week, worth $675 million, to combine its proven automation with OnLogic’s industrial computing expertise. “This acquisition is an important step in advancing our SF2030 vision and our evolution toward GEMBA DX,” stated Junta Tsujinaga, president and CEO of OMRON. “North America is a key growth market for OMRON, and this investment strengthens our foundation there while building the capabilities our customers will increasingly need.” “OnLogic’s industrial computing expertise, flexibility and strong customer relationships complement our strengths in automation and control,” he added. “Together, we see an opportunity to create new value for customers as manufacturing becomes more connected, data-driven and intelligent.” Founded in 1933, OMRON Automation creates, sells, and services fully integrated automation solutions that include sensing , control , safety , vision , and motion . The Kyoto, Japan-based company said its 30,000 employees creatively help businesses solve problems in more than 110 countries. Its Americas office is in Hoffman Estates, Ill. Submit your innovation now! OnLogic to continue computing brand Founded in 2003, OnLogic designs and makes configurable, solution-focused, AI -capable computers engineered for reliability at the Internet of Things (IoT ) edge. The South Burlington, Vt.-based company said it has helped more than 70,000 customers worldwide with their complex computing challenges with systems that are built to order, delivered in days, and designed to last. OnLogic noted that its systems operate in the world’s harshest environments across industries. It said joining OMRON will provide industrial automation expertise and access to new markets. “We built OnLogic to help engineers and innovators solve tough technology challenges by making custom, rugged hardware easy to configure, build, and deploy,” said Sean Larkin, CEO of OnLogic. “Joining OMRON provides the global scale, supply chain depth, and capital resources to accelerate our product roadmaps while preserving our culture, direct sales approach, and operations around the world. Together, we are giving our customers the tools they need to deploy physical AI with confidence.” Following the acquisition, OnLogic will continue to operate as an independent business within the OMRON Group. It will keep its offices in the U.S., the Netherlands, Germany, Taiwan, and Malaysia, as well as its brand identity and direct sales model. OnLogic’s management team, led by Larkin, will remain in place to drive day-to-day operations and strategic growth. OMRON sees opportunities for manufacturers The companies said they will help customers address increasingly complex applications that require greater processing power, connectivity, and intelligence at the edge. OMRON has experience in control, robotics, and safety. OnLogic brings configurable computing platforms designed for demanding applications and environments, as well as its flexible build-to-order model and customer reach across manufacturing and other markets. The companies said they expect to more closely connect machine data, edge computing, and AI with real-time automation and control. Over time, the combination is expected to create systems that help turn data, insights, and AI into faster, more informed actions to optimize manufacturing. OMRON added that the acquisition is an investment in its Industrial Automation Business and strengthens the company’s position in the Americas and Europe . OnLogic has relationships with customers across both traditional automation markets and industries where OMRON sees additional opportunities for growth. In addition, OMRON said it remains committed to its established channel strategy and to continuing to invest in and support the partners that help it serve customers and grow in the market. The companies said they expect the acquisition to close in or around January 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Tell Us What You Think! Cancel reply This site uses Akismet to reduce spam. selectedItems.summary: GXO Logistics, which has tested humanoid robots from multiple companies, will deploy Agility's Digit at two more sites. The post Agility and GXO Logistics plan expanded deployment of Digit humanoid appeared first on The Robot Report .
selectedItems.articleText: Agility and GXO have been collaborating since 2023. Source: Agility Robotics Agility Robotics and GXO Logistics today said they are expanding their partnership to deploy Agility’s Digit humanoid robot in GXO sites in North Carolina and Tennessee. “GXO was the first customer to put Digit to work in live operations under a commercial agreement, and expanding to additional sites is the clearest signal that the value is real,” stated Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility. “Customers are moving beyond asking whether humanoid robots can work to deciding where they can scale them. Years of experience performing real work in GXO’s operations have shaped how we build, deploy and support Digit, and we’re focused on disciplined execution as we grow this partnership.” Founded in 2015, Agility Robotics said it has more than 65,000 hours of real-world operation working with industry safety standards. The Salem, Ore.-based company recently got U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approval for its planned merger with special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC ) Churchill Capital Corp. XI as it prepares to go public. In 2024, Digit earned Agility the inaugural RBR50 Robot of the Year award for being one of the first humanoids to enter commercial trials. It received 2026 honors for moving more than 100,000 totes for GXO last year. This month, the company chose Nyobolt for fast charging , expanded its partnership with NVIDIA, and said it plans to deploy Digit at an AGCO factory for agricultural equipment in 2027. Submit your innovation now! GXO and Agility continue collaboration Spun out of XPO Inc. in 2021, GXO Logistics claimed that it is “the world’s largest pure-play contract logistics provider.” The third-party logistics provider (3PL ) has more than 150,000 employees across over 1,000 facilities, totaling more than 200 million sq. ft. (18.5 million sq. m). The Greenwich, Conn.-based company last month partnered with Exotec to automate fulfillment for Guess in the Netherlands, and like Agility , its executives participated in keynote panels last week’s RoboBusiness event. GXO and Agility first deployed Digit in late 2023 in at a facility in Flowery Branch, Ga. The companies asserted that it was the industry’s first commercial deployment of humanoid robots in live operations and the first robotics-as-a-service (RaaS ) agreement for humanoid robots. Since then, Digit has moved more than 100,000 totes at the Flowery Branch facility, demonstrating its ability to perform repetitive material handling tasks reliably in an active logistics environment. The robot uses the Agility Arc cloud-based fleet management and integration platform. It has worked alongside existing automation to move totes and place them onto conveyors. “Innovation is most powerful when it delivers practical solutions that create value for our customers and our people,” said GXO CEO Patrick Kelleher. “Our partnership with Agility Robotics has been defined by a shared commitment to turning emerging technologies into real-world operational advantage. Together, we’ve helped pioneer the use of humanoid robotics in the warehouse and this expansion reflects our confidence in the technology’s ability to create measurable value for our customers and a better working environment for our teams.” Digit will move from handling bins to more applications. Source: Agility GXO Logistics has tested other humanoids GXO has also tested humanoid robots including Apollo from Apptronik and Reflex from Reflex Robotics . In the company’s second-quarter earnings call in August, Kelleher acknowledged that it had not yet deployed humanoids in production, nor had they produced a return on investment (ROI). “We’ve done 45 pilots on humanoids so far. We have an additional pilot launching in Europe very shortly,” he said at the time. “We have not achieved ROI on humanoids yet. I think we are a couple of years away from that, but we’re seeing such great progress with our partners around the efficacy of that technology and the application opportunities that it has in the warehouse environment.” GXO did not say how much it is investing in the Digit expansion or when and if it expects ROI. The Robot Report has reached out and will share any additional comment or clarification. Partners plan to deploy Digit to more U.S. sites Under the expanded agreement, Digit will support e-commerce fulfillment at GXO sites in Statesville, Tenn., and Lebanon, Ind. The companies said they expect to begin deployments of Digit 4 in in early 2027. Digit 5, which Agility unveiled last month, is designed with new legs, to operate safely near people, and to address a wider range of industrial workflows. GXO said it will migrate to Digit 5 when it becomes commercially available. “The expansion reflects GXO’s long-standing approach to advancing warehouse automation through practical implementation at scale,” said GXO. “As an industry leader in advanced automation and physical AI, GXO partners with leading technology developers to test, refine and deploy emerging solutions in live operating environments. The expanded partnership underscores GXO’s and Agility’s shared commitment to accelerating innovation through real-world application and continuous learning.” Agility also noted that it has invested in infrastructure to manufacture, deploy, and support humanoid robots at scale, including its 70,000 sq. ft. (6,503.2 sq. m) RoboFab facility to manufacture up to 10,000 robots per year. The company has also expanded software and service capabilities, as well as announced plans for a new 50,000 sq. ft. (4,645 sq. m) facility in Pittsburgh to support commercial deployments. A spokesperson told The Robot Report that Agility has paid programs with a global automaker, a major automotive component supplier, and a global consumer products maker. The company said it has more than 30 prospective customers in its pipeline across manufacturing, logistics, aerospace, defense, and consumer products.
